themes_detail.label: Lead exposure spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints in Sunset Park jumped to 10 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 3.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 186% spike (z-score: 4.6)—suggesting either a localized contamination incident, renovation activity releasing lead dust, or new resident awareness of lead hazards in aging housing stock.
evidence: 10 lead complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (186% increase, z-score: 4.6)
Lead spike is the most recently accelerating issue in the district with highest recency signal
Sunset Park has aging housing stock (many pre-1978 buildings) where lead paint and plumbing are endemic concerns
reporting_angles: Investigate whether a specific building renovation or demolition triggered lead dust complaints; cross-reference DOB permit filings (681 active alterations filed recently)
Interview residents and NYC Health Dept about lead testing availability and whether families are proactively checking homes as school year begins

themes_detail.label: Boiler failure crisis
themes_detail.summary: Boiler complaints exploded to 3 cases 3 weeks ago—a 2300% spike from the 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69, severity: high)—indicating a potential cluster of heating failures heading into fall, critical for vulnerable populations in a rent-burdened neighborhood.
evidence: 3 boiler complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Boiler failures occur in fall/winter months when residents depend on heat; timing suggests seasonal escalation beginning
Heat/hot water is already the 3rd highest complaint category overall (630 complaints over 90 days), indicating systemic housing quality issues
reporting_angles: Track whether boiler failures are concentrated in specific buildings or neighborhoods within CD 307; interview HPD about enforcement actions for heat code violations
Profile elderly and low-income residents facing heating shutdowns during transition to cooler weather; assess city's emergency heat response readiness

themes_detail.label: Commercial noise surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints spiked to 50 last week—a 264% increase from the 13.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.67)—suggesting either new commercial activity, late-night venues, or construction, affecting residential quality of life in this mixed-use district.
evidence: 50 noise-commercial complaints last week vs. 13.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (264% increase, z-score: 5.67)
Commercial noise represents a sharp departure from baseline and a distinct signal separate from residential noise (691 complaints, stable trend)
4 active rezonings/land use applications in pipeline (364 Coney Island Ave, Prospect Farm, Brooklyn CD 7 Walk to Park, 783 Fourth Ave) may be driving new commercial development
reporting_angles: Map commercial noise complaints to identify which blocks/venues are generating the surge; cross-reference with recent liquor license approvals, food vendor permits, or construction sites
Interview residents and business owners about what changed recently—new bar, restaurant expansion, late-night food service, or construction noise from development projects

themes_detail.label: Mobile food vendor complaints
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints jumped to 4 last week—a 1500% spike from the 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.66)—indicating either an influx of unpermitted street food operations, code violations, or sanitation concerns that warrant enforcement investigation.
evidence: 4 mobile food vendor complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66)
This is a newly emergent issue with almost no baseline activity, suggesting rapid change in street vendor landscape
May correlate with incoming commercial rezoning activity or shift in enforcement priorities
reporting_angles: Identify which food vendors are generating complaints; determine whether they are properly permitted and inspected by DOHMH
Assess whether this reflects enforcement crackdown, actual increase in street vending, or resident complaints about specific vendors (sanitation, noise, obstruction)

themes_detail.label: Drug activity cluster
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints spiked to 5 cases 3 weeks ago—a 700% increase from the 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.29, severity: high)—signaling possible open-air drug market activity or enforcement attention on specific locations.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase, z-score: 6.29)
Drug activity is normally a very low-volume complaint type, making this spike statistically extreme and noteworthy
Timing (3 weeks ago) suggests sustained concern rather than isolated incident; needs current follow-up to see if trend continues
reporting_angles: Geo-map the 5 drug activity complaints to identify if they cluster on specific blocks or parks; interview NYPD and local precinct about enforcement activity and root causes
Interview community leaders, local business owners, and residents about whether they've noticed increased visible drug use, dealing, or related quality-of-life issues
